description: Computer Knowledge - Computer Software question bank derived from FDA_SDA_Computer_Knowledge_18_3_Computer_Software.pdf. Covers system software, application software, utility software, operating systems, and device drivers. Designed for KEA FDA/SDA examination preparation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is computer software?

options.A: The physical components of a computer
options.B: A collection of programs, procedures and related instructions or data that tell computer hardware how to perform tasks

questions.explanation: Computer software is a collection of programs, procedures and related instructions or data that tell computer hardware how to perform tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is software necessary for a computer?

options.A: It provides the instructions that make hardware useful and controls hardware operations
options.B: It increases the physical size of the computer
options.C: It replaces the need for hardware
options.D: It only helps in playing games

questions.explanation: Software provides the instructions that make hardware useful. It controls hardware operations, manages resources and enables users to perform tasks such as writing documents, calculations and communication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer program?

options.A: A physical component of the computer
options.B: An organised set of instructions written in a programming language or represented in executable form to make a computer perform a specific task

questions.explanation: A computer program is an organised set of instructions written in a programming language or represented in executable form to make a computer perform a specific task.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware consists of physical components, whereas software consists of programs and instructions
options.B: Hardware is always faster than software
options.C: Software is physical and hardware is non-physical
options.D: There is no difference between hardware and software

questions.explanation: Hardware consists of the physical components of a computer, whereas software consists of programs and instructions. Hardware performs operations under the direction of software, and software requires hardware to execute.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the major categories of software?

options.A: System software and application software

questions.explanation: The broad categories commonly taught are system software and application software. Utility software is often treated as a category of system software, while device drivers and operating systems are also forms of system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between system software and application software?

options.A: System software manages computer hardware and provides a platform for other programs; application software helps users perform specific tasks
options.B: System software is used only for games; application software is used only for business
options.C: System software is always free; application software is always paid
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: System software manages computer hardware and provides a platform for other programs; examples include operating systems and device drivers. Application software helps users perform specific tasks; examples include word processors and web browsers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is utility software?

options.A: Software designed to maintain, protect, configure, analyse or optimise a computer system
options.B: Software used only for writing documents
options.C: Software that is always a game
options.D: Software that replaces the operating system

questions.explanation: Utility software is software designed to maintain, protect, configure, analyse or optimise a computer system. Examples include antivirus tools, backup utilities, disk-management tools and file-compression programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is utility software system software or application software?

options.A: It is generally classified as a type or category of system software

questions.explanation: Utility software is generally classified as a type or category of system software because it supports the maintenance and operation of the computer system. Some utilities are also distributed as user-facing applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is firmware?

options.A: Software stored in non-volatile memory within a hardware device and used to control that device at a low level
options.C: A physical component of the CPU

questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory within a hardware device and used to control that device at a low level. Examples include firmware in a motherboard, router, printer or embedded controller.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between software and firmware?

options.A: Software is a broad term for programs and instructions; firmware is a specialised form of software closely associated with controlling a hardware device and commonly stored in non-volatile memory
options.B: Firmware is hardware and software is not
options.C: Software is stored only in ROM and firmware is stored only in RAM
options.D: There is no difference between software and firmware

questions.explanation: Software is a broad term for programs and instructions. Firmware is a specialised form of software closely associated with controlling a hardware device and is commonly stored in non-volatile memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is open-source software?

options.A: Software whose source code is made available under a licence that permits users to inspect, use, modify and redistribute it
options.B: Software that is always free of cost
options.D: Software that only runs on open hardware

questions.explanation: Open-source software is software whose source code is made available under a licence that permits users to inspect, use, modify and redistribute it according to the licence terms.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is proprietary software?

options.A: Software controlled by an individual or organisation under licence terms that restrict access to, modification of or redistribution of its source code or copies
options.C: Software whose source code is always public

questions.explanation: Proprietary software is software controlled by an individual or organisation under licence terms that restrict access to, modification of or redistribution of its source code or copies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is freeware?

options.A: Software made available for use without a purchase price
options.B: Software that is always open source
options.C: Software that cannot be used for free
options.D: Software that is only for servers

questions.explanation: Freeware is software made available for use without a purchase price. Freeware is not necessarily open source; its source code and modification rights may remain restricted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is shareware?

options.A: Software distributed for trial or limited use, often with a requirement to pay for continued use or additional features
options.B: Software that is always free and open source
options.C: Software that is only used for sharing files

questions.explanation: Shareware is software distributed for trial or limited use, often with a requirement to pay for continued use or additional features.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is public-domain software?

options.A: Software for which copyright restrictions have been waived or no longer apply, allowing use without copyright-based restrictions
options.C: Software that is only used by the government

questions.explanation: Public-domain software is software for which copyright restrictions have been waived or no longer apply, allowing use without copyright-based restrictions. The exact legal status depends on jurisdiction and how the work was released.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software licence?

options.A: A legal agreement that sets out the conditions under which software may be installed, used, copied, modified or distributed
options.B: A physical key to start a computer

questions.explanation: A software licence is a legal agreement that sets out the conditions under which software may be installed, used, copied, modified or distributed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is software installation?

options.A: The process of placing program files and required components on a computer and configuring them so that the program can run
options.B: The process of deleting software from a computer
options.C: The process of writing a program

questions.explanation: Software installation is the process of placing program files and required components on a computer and configuring them so that the program can run.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is software updating?

options.A: The process of replacing or modifying installed software components to fix defects, improve security, add features or maintain compatibility
options.B: The process of installing software for the first time

questions.explanation: Software updating is the process of replacing or modifying installed software components to fix defects, improve security, add features or maintain compatibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software patch?

options.A: A targeted update that corrects a defect, addresses a security vulnerability or makes a limited improvement to an existing software product
options.B: A new major version of software

questions.explanation: A software patch is a targeted update that corrects a defect, addresses a security vulnerability or makes a limited improvement to an existing software product.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software version?

options.A: An identified release or state of a software product

questions.explanation: A software version is an identified release or state of a software product. Version numbers help users distinguish releases and determine compatibility or update status.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is system software?

options.A: Software that manages and controls computer hardware and provides the basic environment or platform on which application programs operate
options.C: Software used only for word processing

questions.explanation: System software is the software that manages and controls computer hardware and provides the basic environment or platform on which application programs operate.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main functions of system software?

options.A: Managing processor time, memory, files, storage, input/output devices, security and system resources, and providing services needed by application programs

questions.explanation: System software manages processor time, memory, files, storage, input/output devices, security and system resources, and provides services needed by application programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of system software?

options.A: Operating systems, device drivers, language translators, firmware and system utilities
options.B: Word processors, spreadsheets and presentation programs

questions.explanation: Examples of system software include operating systems, device drivers, language translators, firmware and system utilities.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an operating system?

options.A: System software that manages a computer's hardware and software resources and provides common services and an interface for users and application programs
options.B: A type of application software used for word processing

questions.explanation: An operating system is system software that manages a computer's hardware and software resources and provides common services and an interface for users and application programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a device driver?

options.A: System software that enables the operating system to communicate with and control a particular hardware device or class of devices

questions.explanation: A device driver is system software that enables the operating system to communicate with and control a particular hardware device or class of devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is language translation software?

options.A: Software that converts source code or other program representations into a form that a computer can execute or interpret

questions.explanation: Language translation software converts source code or other program representations into a form that a computer can execute or interpret. Examples include assemblers, compilers and interpreters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an assembler?

options.A: System software that translates assembly-language instructions into machine code or object code for a processor

questions.explanation: An assembler is system software that translates assembly-language instructions into machine code or object code for a processor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a compiler?

options.A: Software that translates a program written in a high-level language into machine code, object code or another lower-level representation before execution
options.B: Software that executes instructions at runtime without compilation

questions.explanation: A compiler translates a program written in a high-level language into machine code, object code or another lower-level representation before the resulting program is executed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an interpreter?

options.A: Software that executes a program by analysing and carrying out its instructions at runtime
options.B: Software that translates assembly language into machine code

questions.explanation: An interpreter executes a program by analysing and carrying out its instructions at runtime, often statement by statement or through an intermediate representation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter?

options.A: A traditional compiler translates source code into a target program or object code before execution, whereas an interpreter carries out program instructions at runtime
options.B: A compiler executes code at runtime and an interpreter translates before execution
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A compiler is hardware and an interpreter is software

questions.explanation: A traditional compiler translates source code into a target program or object code before execution, whereas an interpreter carries out program instructions at runtime. Modern language implementations may combine compilation and interpretation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an operating-system kernel?

options.A: The central component of an operating system that manages core functions such as processes, memory, files and devices

questions.explanation: The kernel is the central component of an operating system. It manages core functions such as processes, memory, files and devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shell in an operating system?

options.A: A user interface or command interpreter through which users or programs request operating-system services
options.B: A physical case that holds the computer

questions.explanation: A shell is a user interface or command interpreter through which users or programs request operating-system services. It may be command-line based or graphical, depending on the system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a command-line interface (CLI)?

options.A: A text-based interface in which a user enters commands to interact with an operating system or program
options.B: A graphical interface with windows and icons

questions.explanation: A CLI is a text-based interface in which a user enters commands to interact with an operating system or program.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a graphical user interface (GUI)?

options.A: An interface that allows users to interact with a computer through graphical elements such as windows, icons, menus, buttons and pointers

questions.explanation: A GUI is an interface that allows users to interact with a computer through graphical elements such as windows, icons, menus, buttons and pointers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between GUI and CLI?

options.A: A GUI uses graphical elements and pointing or touch interaction, whereas a CLI uses typed commands
options.B: A GUI uses typed commands and a CLI uses graphical elements
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A GUI is hardware and a CLI is software

questions.explanation: A GUI uses graphical elements and pointing or touch interaction, whereas a CLI uses typed commands. A CLI can be efficient for automation and administration, while a GUI can be easier for many visual tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is application software?

options.A: Software designed to help users perform specific tasks, such as preparing documents, calculating figures, browsing the internet, editing images or managing records
options.C: Software that is always part of the operating system

questions.explanation: Application software is software designed to help users perform specific tasks, such as preparing documents, calculating figures, browsing the internet, editing images or managing records.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the two broad categories of application software?

options.A: General-purpose or packaged applications and special-purpose or customised applications

questions.explanation: Application software is commonly grouped into general-purpose or packaged applications and special-purpose or customised applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is general-purpose application software?

options.A: Software designed to perform common tasks for many users, such as word processors, spreadsheets, presentation programs, database applications and web browsers
options.B: Software designed for a particular task such as railway reservation

questions.explanation: General-purpose application software is designed to perform common tasks for many users. Examples include word processors, spreadsheets, presentation programs, database applications and web browsers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is special-purpose application software?

options.A: Software designed for a particular task or a narrow set of tasks, such as railway reservation, payroll processing, billing or hospital management
options.B: Software designed for common tasks for many users

questions.explanation: Special-purpose application software is designed for a particular task or a narrow set of tasks, such as railway reservation, payroll processing, billing or hospital management.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is customised or tailor-made software?

options.A: Software developed or configured to meet the specific requirements of a particular user or organisation
options.B: Software developed for the mass market
options.D: Software that is part of the operating system

questions.explanation: Customised software is developed or configured to meet the specific requirements of a particular user or organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a word-processing application?

options.A: Software used to create, edit, format, save and print text documents
options.B: Software used to perform calculations in rows and columns
options.C: Software used to create slide presentations
options.D: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: A word-processing application is software used to create, edit, format, save and print text documents. Examples include Microsoft Word and LibreOffice Writer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spreadsheet software?

options.A: Software that organises data in rows and columns and supports calculations, formulas, functions, charts and data analysis
options.B: Software used to create text documents
options.C: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: Spreadsheet software organises data in rows and columns and supports calculations, formulas, functions, charts and data analysis. Examples include Microsoft Excel and LibreOffice Calc.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is presentation software?

options.A: Software used to create and display slide-based presentations containing text, images, charts, audio, video and animations
options.C: Software used to browse the web

questions.explanation: Presentation software is used to create and display slide-based presentations containing text, images, charts, audio, video and animations. Examples include Microsoft PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is database application software?

options.A: Software used to create, store, organise, retrieve and manage structured data
options.B: Software used to create text documents
options.D: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: Database application software is used to create, store, organise, retrieve and manage structured data. Examples include database-management systems such as Microsoft Access, MySQL and PostgreSQL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a web browser?

options.A: Application software used to access, retrieve and display information and resources on the World Wide Web

questions.explanation: A web browser is application software used to access, retrieve and display information and resources on the World Wide Web. Examples include Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge and Apple Safari.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email-client software?

options.A: Application software used to compose, send, receive, organise and search email messages
options.B: Software used to browse the web

questions.explanation: An email client is application software used to compose, send, receive, organise and search email messages. It may access email through protocols or services such as IMAP, POP3 and SMTP.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is graphics software?

options.A: Software used to create, edit or manipulate images, illustrations and visual designs

questions.explanation: Graphics software is used to create, edit or manipulate images, illustrations and visual designs. Examples include raster-image editors, vector-graphics editors and computer-aided design tools.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multimedia software?

options.A: Software used to create, edit, play or manage combinations of media such as text, images, audio, video and animation
options.B: Software used only for text documents

questions.explanation: Multimedia software is used to create, edit, play or manage combinations of media such as text, images, audio, video and animation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is accounting software?

options.A: Software that supports financial tasks such as recording transactions, maintaining ledgers, preparing invoices, managing accounts and generating financial reports
options.C: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: Accounting software supports financial tasks such as recording transactions, maintaining ledgers, preparing invoices, managing accounts and generating financial reports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is payroll software?

options.A: Software that calculates employee wages, deductions and net pay, and helps prepare payroll records and related reports
options.C: Software used to browse the web

questions.explanation: Payroll software calculates employee wages, deductions and net pay, and helps prepare payroll records and related reports according to applicable rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is educational software?

options.A: Software that supports teaching and learning through digital lessons, tutorials, practice exercises, simulations, assessments and learning-management systems

questions.explanation: Educational software supports teaching and learning through digital lessons, tutorials, practice exercises, simulations, assessments and learning-management systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is enterprise application software?

options.A: Software that supports organisation-wide business processes, such as finance, human resources, supply chains, customer management and enterprise resource planning
options.B: Software used only for personal tasks
options.D: Software used only for web browsing

questions.explanation: Enterprise application software supports organisation-wide business processes, such as finance, human resources, supply chains, customer management and enterprise resource planning.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an ERP system?

options.A: Enterprise Resource Planning system that integrates major organisational processes and data within a coordinated software system

questions.explanation: ERP stands for Enterprise Resource Planning. An ERP system integrates major organisational processes and data, such as finance, procurement, inventory, production and human resources, within a coordinated software system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a CRM system?

options.A: Customer Relationship Management system that helps an organisation manage customer information, interactions, sales activities and customer-service processes

questions.explanation: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management. A CRM system helps an organisation manage customer information, interactions, sales activities and customer-service processes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between packaged software and customised software?

options.A: Packaged software is developed for a broad market and is generally supplied with standard features, whereas customised software is designed or adapted to meet particular user or organisational requirements
options.B: Packaged software is always free and customised software is always paid
options.C: Packaged software is hardware and customised software is software
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Packaged software is developed for a broad market and is generally supplied with standard features, whereas customised software is designed or adapted to meet particular user or organisational requirements.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can application software run without an operating system?

options.A: Most ordinary desktop and mobile application software relies on an operating system or runtime environment; some specialised programs run directly on hardware or in embedded environments
options.B: Yes, all application software can run without an operating system
options.C: No, application software can never run without an operating system
options.D: Application software is the same as an operating system

questions.explanation: Most ordinary desktop and mobile application software relies on an operating system or runtime environment. Some specialised programs run directly on hardware or in embedded environments without a conventional general-purpose OS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is utility software?

options.A: Software that performs maintenance, protection, configuration, monitoring or optimisation tasks that help keep a computer system secure and operating effectively
options.B: Software used only for word processing
options.D: Software that replaces the operating system

questions.explanation: Utility software performs maintenance, protection, configuration, monitoring or optimisation tasks that help keep a computer system secure and operating effectively.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are common examples of utility software?

options.A: Antivirus programs, firewalls, backup tools, file-compression utilities, disk-cleanup tools, disk-management tools, encryption tools and system-monitoring utilities

questions.explanation: Common examples of utility software include antivirus programs, firewalls, backup tools, file-compression utilities, disk-cleanup tools, disk-management tools, encryption tools and system-monitoring utilities.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is antivirus software?

options.A: A security utility designed to detect, block, quarantine or remove malicious software
options.C: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: Antivirus software is a security utility designed to detect, block, quarantine or remove malicious software. Modern endpoint-protection tools may also use behavioural analysis and other security techniques.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is malware?

options.A: Malicious software designed to harm, disrupt, spy on, gain unauthorised access to or otherwise misuse a computer system or its data
options.B: Software used to protect a computer

questions.explanation: Malware is malicious software designed to harm, disrupt, spy on, gain unauthorised access to or otherwise misuse a computer system or its data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer virus?

options.A: A type of malware that attaches itself to a legitimate file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed or otherwise activated

questions.explanation: A computer virus is a type of malware that attaches itself to a legitimate file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed or otherwise activated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer worm?

options.A: Malware that can self-replicate and spread between systems, often across networks, without needing to attach itself to a host program

questions.explanation: A computer worm is malware that can self-replicate and spread between systems, often across networks, without needing to attach itself to a host program.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Trojan horse?

options.A: Malware that disguises itself as or is presented as legitimate software to trick users into installing or running it

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse is malware that disguises itself as or is presented as legitimate software to trick users into installing or running it. Unlike a virus or worm, it does not inherently self-replicate.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spyware?

options.A: Software that secretly monitors user activity or collects information without appropriate consent, potentially compromising privacy and security
options.B: Software used to protect a computer

questions.explanation: Spyware is software that secretly monitors user activity or collects information without appropriate consent, potentially compromising privacy and security.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a firewall?

options.A: A security system, implemented in hardware, software or both, that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined security rules
options.B: A physical wall that protects computers

questions.explanation: A firewall is a security system, implemented in hardware, software or both, that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined security rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a backup utility?

options.A: Software that creates or manages copies of files, folders, system data or entire systems so that information can be restored after loss, corruption or failure
options.C: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: A backup utility creates or manages copies of files, folders, system data or entire systems so that information can be restored after loss, corruption or failure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file-compression software?

options.A: Software that reduces the size of files or groups of files to save storage space or reduce transfer time
options.C: Software used to browse the internet

questions.explanation: File-compression software reduces the size of files or groups of files to save storage space or reduce transfer time. Examples of common archive formats include ZIP and 7z.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between lossless and lossy compression?

options.A: Lossless compression allows the original data to be reconstructed exactly, whereas lossy compression permanently removes some information to achieve greater size reduction
options.B: Lossless compression removes data and lossy compression preserves all data
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Lossless compression is only for images and lossy compression is only for text

questions.explanation: Lossless compression allows the original data to be reconstructed exactly, whereas lossy compression permanently removes some information to achieve greater size reduction. ZIP is commonly lossless; JPEG image compression is commonly lossy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is disk-cleanup software?

options.A: Software that identifies and helps remove unnecessary files, such as temporary files and selected caches, to free storage space

questions.explanation: Disk-cleanup software identifies and helps remove unnecessary files, such as temporary files and selected caches, to free storage space. Users should avoid deleting files whose purpose they do not understand.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is disk-defragmentation software?

options.A: A utility that rearranges fragmented file data to improve sequential access on traditional HDDs
options.B: A utility that deletes all files from a disk

questions.explanation: A disk-defragmentation utility rearranges fragmented file data to improve sequential access on traditional HDDs. SSDs generally do not require traditional defragmentation; operating systems use SSD-specific optimisation such as TRIM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is disk-partitioning software?

options.A: Software that creates, deletes, resizes or manages partitions on a storage device

questions.explanation: Disk-partitioning software creates, deletes, resizes or manages partitions on a storage device. Partition changes can cause data loss if performed incorrectly, so backups are important.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is encryption software?

options.A: Software that converts readable data (plaintext) into an encoded form (ciphertext) using a cryptographic method and key

questions.explanation: Encryption software converts readable data (plaintext) into an encoded form (ciphertext) using a cryptographic method and key, so that only authorised parties with the required key can decrypt it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file manager?

options.A: Software that allows users to browse, create, copy, move, rename, organise and delete files and folders

questions.explanation: A file manager is software that allows users to browse, create, copy, move, rename, organise and delete files and folders.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a system-monitoring utility?

options.A: A utility that displays information about system performance and resource use, such as CPU activity, memory use, storage activity, temperature or network traffic
options.C: A utility that browses the internet

questions.explanation: A system-monitoring utility displays information about system performance and resource use, such as CPU activity, memory use, storage activity, temperature or network traffic.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of a backup and restore utility?

options.A: A backup utility creates recovery copies, while a restore function uses those copies to recover files, settings or a system after accidental deletion, corruption or failure
options.B: A backup utility deletes files and a restore function creates new files
options.C: A backup utility encrypts files and a restore function decrypts them
options.D: A backup utility compresses files and a restore function decompresses them

questions.explanation: A backup utility creates recovery copies, while a restore function uses those copies to recover files, settings or a system after accidental deletion, corruption or failure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an operating system (OS)?

options.A: System software that acts as an intermediary between users or application programs and computer hardware, managing resources and providing common services

questions.explanation: An operating system is system software that acts as an intermediary between users or application programs and computer hardware, managing resources and providing common services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main objectives of an operating system?

options.A: To make the computer convenient to use, manage hardware resources efficiently, provide a stable environment for programs and help protect system data and operations
options.C: To browse the internet and send emails

questions.explanation: The main objectives of an operating system are to make the computer convenient to use, manage hardware resources efficiently, provide a stable environment for programs and help protect system data and operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the major functions of an operating system?

options.A: Process management, memory management, file management, device and input/output management, storage management, security, user-interface services, networking and error handling
options.B: Only word processing and spreadsheet calculations

questions.explanation: Major functions of an operating system include process management, memory management, file management, device and input/output management, storage management, security, user-interface services, networking and error handling.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is process management?

options.A: The operating-system function that creates, schedules, coordinates and terminates processes and allocates CPU time to them
options.B: The management of files and folders

questions.explanation: Process management is the operating-system function that creates, schedules, coordinates and terminates processes and allocates CPU time to them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a process?

options.A: A program in execution, together with its current state and the resources required for its execution

questions.explanation: A process is a program in execution, together with its current state and the resources required for its execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a thread?

options.A: A unit of execution within a process

questions.explanation: A thread is a unit of execution within a process. A process may contain one or more threads that share certain process resources while having their own execution state.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multitasking in an operating system?

options.A: The ability of an operating system to manage multiple tasks during the same period by scheduling processor time and coordinating resources
options.B: The ability to use multiple processors
options.C: The ability to support multiple users
options.D: The ability to connect to multiple networks

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the ability of an operating system to manage multiple tasks during the same period by scheduling processor time and coordinating resources. On a single-core CPU, tasks may take turns; multicore systems can also execute tasks in parallel.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multiprocessing?

options.A: The use of two or more processing units or CPU cores to execute processes or threads concurrently
options.B: The ability to manage multiple tasks on a single processor
options.C: The ability to support multiple users
options.D: The ability to run multiple operating systems

questions.explanation: Multiprocessing is the use of two or more processing units or CPU cores to execute processes or threads concurrently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is memory management?

options.A: The operating-system function that allocates, tracks and releases main memory for programs and system processes and helps protect the memory spaces of different processes
options.B: The management of files and folders

questions.explanation: Memory management is the operating-system function that allocates, tracks and releases main memory for programs and system processes and helps protect the memory spaces of different processes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is virtual memory?

options.A: A memory-management technique that gives processes a virtual address space and allows the operating system to use secondary storage as backing for some memory contents when needed

questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory-management technique that gives processes a virtual address space and allows the operating system to use secondary storage as backing for some memory contents when needed. It does not make storage as fast as RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file management in an operating system?

options.A: The function that organises files and directories, maintains file names and metadata, controls access permissions and supports operations such as creating, reading, writing, moving and deleting files

questions.explanation: File management organises files and directories, maintains file names and metadata, controls access permissions and supports operations such as creating, reading, writing, moving and deleting files.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file system?

options.A: The method and data structure an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device

questions.explanation: A file system is the method and data structure an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device. Examples include FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, ext4 and APFS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is device management?

options.A: The function that controls and coordinates hardware devices through drivers and operating-system services, allocating access and handling input/output operations
options.B: The management of files and folders

questions.explanation: Device management controls and coordinates hardware devices through drivers and operating-system services, allocating access and handling input/output operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is booting in an operating system?

options.A: The startup process in which firmware initialises hardware, identifies a bootable device and starts a bootloader or operating-system loader, which loads the operating system into memory
options.B: The process of shutting down the computer

questions.explanation: Booting is the startup process in which firmware initialises hardware, identifies a bootable device and starts a bootloader or operating-system loader, which loads the operating system into memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a bootloader?

options.A: A program that helps load the operating system kernel and transfer control to it during the startup process

questions.explanation: A bootloader is a program that helps load the operating system kernel and transfer control to it during the startup process.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user account in an operating system?

options.A: An account that identifies a user or service and determines the permissions, settings and resources available during system use

questions.explanation: A user account identifies a user or service and determines the permissions, settings and resources available during system use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is authentication?

options.A: The process of verifying the identity of a user, device or process, for example through a password, security key, fingerprint or multifactor authentication
options.B: The process of determining what an authenticated user is permitted to access
options.C: The process of creating a user account
options.D: The process of deleting a user account

questions.explanation: Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user, device or process, for example through a password, security key, fingerprint or multifactor authentication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is authorisation?

options.A: The process of determining what an authenticated user or process is permitted to access or do
options.C: The process of creating a user account
options.D: The process of deleting a user account

questions.explanation: Authorisation is the process of determining what an authenticated user or process is permitted to access or do.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?

options.A: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines the permissions granted to that identity
options.B: Authentication determines permissions; authorisation verifies identity
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Authentication is for hardware; authorisation is for software

questions.explanation: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines the permissions granted to that identity.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a system call?

options.A: A controlled interface through which an application requests a service from the operating-system kernel, such as file access, process creation or memory management
options.B: A telephone call made by the system

questions.explanation: A system call is a controlled interface through which an application requests a service from the operating-system kernel, such as file access, process creation or memory management.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a deadlock in an operating system?

options.A: A condition in which two or more processes are permanently waiting for resources held by one another, so none of them can proceed
options.B: A condition in which the computer is turned off
options.C: A condition in which the network is disconnected
options.D: A condition in which the hard disk is full

questions.explanation: A deadlock is a condition in which two or more processes are permanently waiting for resources held by one another, so none of them can proceed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spoofing in the context of operating systems?

options.A: Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line, which places jobs in a queue or temporary storage so a slower peripheral, such as a printer, can process them in sequence while the CPU continues other work
options.B: A security attack that impersonates a user

questions.explanation: Spoofing stands for Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line. It places jobs in a queue or temporary storage so a slower peripheral, such as a printer, can process them in sequence while the CPU continues other work.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between GUI and CLI operating systems?

options.A: An operating system with a GUI provides graphical interaction through windows, icons and menus; a CLI provides text-based command interaction
options.B: A GUI uses typed commands and a CLI uses graphical elements
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A GUI is hardware and a CLI is software

questions.explanation: An operating system with a GUI provides graphical interaction through windows, icons and menus; a CLI provides text-based command interaction. Many modern operating systems support both.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a real-time operating system (RTOS)?

options.A: An operating system designed to respond to events within specified timing constraints
options.B: An operating system that runs only in real time on the internet
options.C: An operating system that is always fast
options.D: An operating system that only supports one user

questions.explanation: A real-time operating system is designed to respond to events within specified timing constraints. Correctness depends not only on the result but also on the time at which the result is produced.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a distributed operating system?

options.A: An operating system that manages resources across multiple networked computers and aims to present them in a coordinated way
options.B: An operating system that runs only on a single computer
options.C: An operating system that is only used for file sharing
options.D: An operating system that is only used for printing

questions.explanation: A distributed operating system manages resources across multiple networked computers and aims to present them in a coordinated way. It is distinct from an ordinary operating system that merely supports networking.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network operating system?

options.A: An operating system that provides services and tools for managing networked computers, users, shared files, printers and other network resources
options.B: An operating system that runs only on a single computer
options.C: An operating system that is only used for gaming
options.D: An operating system that is only used for word processing

questions.explanation: A network operating system provides services and tools for managing networked computers, users, shared files, printers and other network resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a single-user operating system?

options.A: An operating system designed primarily to support one user at a time
options.B: An operating system that supports multiple users simultaneously
options.C: An operating system that supports multiple processors
options.D: An operating system that runs only on servers

questions.explanation: A single-user operating system is designed primarily to support one user at a time. It may still run multiple programs for that user.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a multi-user operating system?

options.A: An operating system that allows multiple users to access system resources, often concurrently, while managing their accounts, processes and permissions
options.B: An operating system that supports only one user at a time
options.C: An operating system that runs only on a single computer
options.D: An operating system that does not support networking

questions.explanation: A multi-user operating system allows multiple users to access system resources, often concurrently, while managing their accounts, processes and permissions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a single-tasking operating system?

options.A: An operating system designed to execute one task or program at a time
options.B: An operating system that can execute multiple tasks at a time
options.C: An operating system that supports multiple users
options.D: An operating system that supports multiple processors

questions.explanation: A single-tasking operating system is designed to execute one task or program at a time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a multitasking operating system?

options.A: An operating system that allows multiple programs or tasks to make progress during the same period by sharing CPU time and system resources
options.B: An operating system that executes only one task at a time
options.C: An operating system that supports only one user
options.D: An operating system that does not support networking

questions.explanation: A multitasking operating system allows multiple programs or tasks to make progress during the same period by sharing CPU time and system resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a batch operating system?

options.A: An operating system that collects jobs and processes them in groups or batches with little or no direct interaction between the user and the job while it runs
options.B: An operating system that provides interactive access to multiple users
options.C: An operating system that supports multiple processors
options.D: An operating system that runs only on mobile devices

questions.explanation: A batch operating system collects jobs and processes them in groups or batches with little or no direct interaction between the user and the job while it runs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a time-sharing operating system?

options.A: An operating system that divides processor time into small intervals and allocates them among multiple users or processes, providing interactive access and the appearance of simultaneous execution
options.B: An operating system that processes jobs in batches
options.C: An operating system that supports only one user
options.D: An operating system that is used only for real-time applications

questions.explanation: A time-sharing operating system divides processor time into small intervals and allocates them among multiple users or processes, providing interactive access and the appearance of simultaneous execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a multiprocessing operating system?

options.A: An operating system that supports a computer with two or more processors or processing cores and can schedule work across them
options.B: An operating system that supports only one processor
options.C: An operating system that supports multiple users
options.D: An operating system that processes jobs in batches

questions.explanation: A multiprocessing operating system supports a computer with two or more processors or processing cores and can schedule work across them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a real-time operating system used for?

options.A: Applications such as industrial control, medical equipment and embedded systems that require predictable responses within specified time limits

questions.explanation: A real-time operating system is designed to provide predictable responses within specified time limits. It is used in applications such as industrial control, medical equipment and embedded systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an embedded operating system?

options.A: An operating system designed for a dedicated computing device with specific functions and often limited resources, such as a router, appliance, vehicle controller or industrial device
options.B: An operating system designed for personal computers
options.C: An operating system designed for servers only
options.D: An operating system designed for mainframes only

questions.explanation: An embedded operating system is designed for a dedicated computing device with specific functions and often limited resources, such as a router, appliance, vehicle controller or industrial device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mobile operating system?

options.A: An operating system designed for portable devices such as smartphones and tablets and manages touch input, wireless communication, applications, power and device hardware
options.B: An operating system designed for desktop computers
options.C: An operating system designed for servers
options.D: An operating system designed for mainframes

questions.explanation: A mobile operating system is designed for portable devices such as smartphones and tablets and manages touch input, wireless communication, applications, power and device hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between batch processing and time-sharing?

options.A: Batch processing runs collected jobs with little user interaction during execution; time-sharing provides interactive access by allocating short CPU time slices among users or processes
options.B: Batch processing provides interactive access; time-sharing runs collected jobs with little user interaction
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Batch processing is for mobile devices; time-sharing is for servers

questions.explanation: Batch processing runs collected jobs with little user interaction during execution; time-sharing provides interactive access by allocating short CPU time slices among users or processes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between multitasking and multiprocessing?

options.A: Multitasking is the management of multiple tasks so they make progress during the same period; multiprocessing uses multiple processing units or cores to execute work concurrently
options.B: Multitasking uses multiple processors; multiprocessing manages multiple tasks on a single processor
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Multitasking is for mobile devices; multiprocessing is for servers

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the management of multiple tasks so they make progress during the same period; multiprocessing uses multiple processing units or cores to execute work concurrently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a multi-user and a multitasking operating system?

options.A: Multi-user describes support for multiple users, while multitasking describes the ability to manage multiple tasks or programs; an operating system can support both
options.B: Multi-user describes the ability to manage multiple tasks; multitasking describes support for multiple users
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Multi-user is for mobile devices; multitasking is for servers

questions.explanation: Multi-user describes support for multiple users, while multitasking describes the ability to manage multiple tasks or programs. An operating system can support both.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Microsoft Windows?

options.A: A family of proprietary operating systems developed by Microsoft and widely used on personal computers and in business environments

questions.explanation: Microsoft Windows is a family of proprietary operating systems developed by Microsoft and widely used on personal computers and in business environments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Linux?

options.A: An open-source, Unix-like operating-system kernel
options.B: A proprietary operating system developed by Microsoft

questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source, Unix-like operating-system kernel. Complete Linux operating systems are commonly distributed as distributions, such as Ubuntu, Fedora and Debian, which combine the kernel with system tools and applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Linux distribution?

options.A: An operating-system package built around the Linux kernel and supplied with system utilities, package-management tools, applications and configuration choices

questions.explanation: A Linux distribution is an operating-system package built around the Linux kernel and supplied with system utilities, package-management tools, applications and configuration choices. Examples include Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Linux Mint.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is UNIX?

options.A: A family of operating systems developed from the original UNIX system and associated standards, associated with multi-user and multitasking capabilities

questions.explanation: UNIX is a family of operating systems developed from the original UNIX system and associated standards. It influenced many modern operating systems and is associated with multi-user and multitasking capabilities.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is macOS?

options.A: Apple's proprietary desktop operating system for Mac computers, based on Darwin which includes a Unix-derived foundation

questions.explanation: macOS is Apple's proprietary desktop operating system for Mac computers. It is based on Darwin, which includes a Unix-derived foundation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Android?

options.A: A mobile operating-system platform based on the Linux kernel and developed primarily by Google and the Android Open Source Project ecosystem
options.B: A desktop operating system developed by Microsoft

questions.explanation: Android is a mobile operating-system platform based on the Linux kernel and developed primarily by Google and the Android Open Source Project ecosystem.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is iOS?

options.A: Apple's mobile operating system used on iPhone devices

questions.explanation: iOS is Apple's mobile operating system used on iPhone devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ChromeOS?

options.A: Google's operating system designed primarily for Chromebook devices, with strong integration of web applications and cloud services while also supporting local applications

questions.explanation: ChromeOS is Google's operating system designed primarily for Chromebook devices, with strong integration of web applications and cloud services while also supporting local applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which operating system is open source among common desktop choices?

options.A: Linux distributions such as Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora

questions.explanation: Linux distributions such as Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora are open-source operating systems. The Linux kernel is open source; Windows and macOS are proprietary.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Are Windows, Linux and macOS operating systems or application software?

options.A: They are operating systems, so they are classified as system software

questions.explanation: Windows, Linux-based distributions and macOS are operating systems, so they are classified as system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Are Microsoft Word and Microsoft Excel operating systems?

options.A: No, Microsoft Word is word-processing application software and Microsoft Excel is spreadsheet application software

questions.explanation: No. Microsoft Word is word-processing application software, and Microsoft Excel is spreadsheet application software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a device driver?

options.A: Software that allows an operating system to identify, communicate with and control a hardware device through a defined interface

questions.explanation: A device driver is software that allows an operating system to identify, communicate with and control a hardware device through a defined interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why are device drivers required?

options.A: Drivers translate operating-system requests into device-specific operations and communicate device status or data back to the operating system
options.B: Drivers are required only for playing games
options.C: Drivers are required only for browsing the internet
options.D: Drivers are required only for word processing

questions.explanation: Drivers translate operating-system requests into device-specific operations and communicate device status or data back to the operating system, allowing hardware and software to work together.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are common examples of device drivers?

options.A: Printer drivers, graphics drivers, audio drivers, network-adapter drivers, Bluetooth drivers, storage-controller drivers and chipset drivers

questions.explanation: Common examples of device drivers include printer drivers, graphics drivers, audio drivers, network-adapter drivers, Bluetooth drivers, storage-controller drivers and chipset drivers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a printer driver?

options.A: Software that enables the operating system and applications to send print jobs in a format and set of commands understood by a particular printer or printer family

questions.explanation: A printer driver is software that enables the operating system and applications to send print jobs in a format and set of commands understood by a particular printer or printer family.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a graphics driver?

options.A: Software that enables the operating system and applications to communicate with a graphics processing unit or display

questions.explanation: A graphics driver enables the operating system and applications to communicate with a graphics processing unit or display.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an audio driver?

options.A: Software that enables the operating system to communicate with sound hardware, such as an audio controller or sound card, for audio input and output

questions.explanation: An audio driver enables the operating system to communicate with sound hardware, such as an audio controller or sound card, for audio input and output.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network driver?

options.A: Software that enables the operating system to communicate with a network interface, such as an Ethernet adapter or Wi-Fi adapter

questions.explanation: A network driver enables the operating system to communicate with a network interface, such as an Ethernet adapter or Wi-Fi adapter.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens if a required device driver is missing or corrupted?

options.A: The hardware may not work, may operate with limited functionality, or may produce errors
options.B: The computer will always work perfectly
options.C: The hardware will automatically fix itself
options.D: The operating system will be deleted

questions.explanation: The hardware may not work, may operate with limited functionality, or may produce errors. Installing a compatible and trusted driver or updating the existing driver can resolve some driver-related problems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Plug and Play (PnP)?

options.A: A technology that allows an operating system to detect and configure supported hardware devices with minimal user intervention, often by identifying the device and loading a suitable driver
options.B: A technology that requires manual configuration of all hardware

questions.explanation: Plug and Play is a technology that allows an operating system to detect and configure supported hardware devices with minimal user intervention, often by identifying the device and loading a suitable driver.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a device driver and an application program?

options.A: A device driver enables the operating system to control or communicate with hardware, whereas an application program performs a task for the user
options.B: A device driver performs tasks for the user; an application program controls hardware
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A device driver is hardware; an application program is software

questions.explanation: A device driver enables the operating system to control or communicate with hardware, whereas an application program performs a task for the user, such as editing a document or browsing the web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Are device drivers hardware or software?

options.A: Device drivers are software, specifically system software

questions.explanation: Device drivers are software, specifically system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Should drivers be downloaded from unknown websites?

options.A: No, drivers should be obtained from the device manufacturer, computer manufacturer or a trusted operating-system update service
options.B: Yes, any website is safe for drivers
options.C: Yes, unknown websites provide the best drivers
options.D: Drivers do not need to be downloaded

questions.explanation: No. Drivers should be obtained from the device manufacturer, computer manufacturer or a trusted operating-system update service to reduce the risk of malware, incompatibility and incorrect installation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software manages the computer's hardware resources?

options.A: System software, especially the operating system

questions.explanation: System software, especially the operating system, manages the computer's hardware resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software is designed to perform user-oriented tasks?

options.A: Application software

questions.explanation: Application software is designed to perform user-oriented tasks such as word processing, calculations and browsing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software is used to protect a computer against malware?

options.A: Antivirus or endpoint-protection software

questions.explanation: Antivirus or endpoint-protection software is a security utility used to detect, block or remove malware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software manages files and folders?

options.A: The operating system provides file-management functions, and a file-manager utility or application gives users an interface to perform file operations

questions.explanation: The operating system provides file-management functions, and a file-manager utility or application gives users an interface to perform file operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software allows the operating system to communicate with a printer?

options.A: A printer driver

questions.explanation: A printer driver allows the operating system to communicate with and control a compatible printer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software converts a high-level language program into object code before execution in the traditional model?

options.A: A compiler

questions.explanation: A compiler translates high-level source code into object code or another target representation before execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software translates assembly language into machine code?

options.A: An assembler

questions.explanation: An assembler translates assembly-language instructions into machine code or object code.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which software executes instructions at runtime without the traditional requirement to compile the entire source program into a standalone executable first?

options.A: An interpreter

questions.explanation: An interpreter executes program instructions at runtime, although modern language systems may also use intermediate code and just-in-time compilation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which category includes Windows, Linux distributions and macOS?

options.A: They are operating systems and are classified as system software

questions.explanation: They are operating systems and are classified as system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which category includes word processors, spreadsheets and presentation programs?

options.A: They are application software

questions.explanation: They are application software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which category includes antivirus, backup and disk-cleanup tools?

options.A: They are utility software, generally considered a category of system software

questions.explanation: They are utility software, generally considered a category of system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of software is stored in a device to control its basic operation?

options.A: Firmware

questions.explanation: Firmware is stored in non-volatile memory and controls basic device operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between a virus and a worm?

options.A: A virus attaches to a host file or program and spreads when the host is activated; a worm can self-replicate and spread independently across systems or networks
options.B: A virus self-replicates independently; a worm attaches to a host file
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A virus is hardware; a worm is software

questions.explanation: A virus attaches to a host file or program and spreads when the host is activated; a worm can self-replicate and spread independently across systems or networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between a Trojan horse and a virus?

options.A: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software to deceive users and does not inherently self-replicate; a virus attaches to a host and replicates when activated
options.B: A Trojan horse self-replicates; a virus does not
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A Trojan horse is hardware; a virus is software

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software to deceive users and does not inherently self-replicate; a virus attaches to a host and replicates when activated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between freeware and open-source software?

options.A: Freeware is available without a purchase price but may have closed source and restrictive terms; open-source software provides source-code access and rights defined by its licence
options.B: Freeware provides source code; open-source software does not
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Freeware is always open source; open-source software is always paid

questions.explanation: Freeware is available without a purchase price but may have closed source and restrictive terms; open-source software provides source-code access and rights defined by its licence.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between an update and an upgrade?

options.A: An update generally applies fixes, security improvements or smaller enhancements to an existing version; an upgrade usually moves to a newer major version or a more substantial release
options.B: An update moves to a new major version; an upgrade applies small fixes
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: An update is for hardware; an upgrade is for software

questions.explanation: An update generally applies fixes, security improvements or smaller enhancements to an existing version; an upgrade usually moves to a newer major version or a more substantial release. Vendors may use these terms differently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does OS stand for?

options.A: Operating System

questions.explanation: OS stands for Operating System.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does GUI stand for?

options.A: Graphical User Interface

questions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does CLI stand for?

options.A: Command-Line Interface

questions.explanation: CLI stands for Command-Line Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does BIOS stand for?

options.A: Basic Input/Output System

questions.explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input/Output System. It is motherboard firmware used to initialise hardware and begin the boot process; modern systems commonly use UEFI.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does UEFI stand for?

options.A: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface

questions.explanation: UEFI stands for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does ERP stand for?

options.A: Enterprise Resource Planning

questions.explanation: ERP stands for Enterprise Resource Planning.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does CRM stand for?

options.A: Customer Relationship Management

questions.explanation: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does RTOS stand for?

options.A: Real-Time Operating System

questions.explanation: RTOS stands for Real-Time Operating System.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does PnP stand for?

options.A: Plug and Play

questions.explanation: PnP stands for Plug and Play.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does GPL stand for?

options.A: GNU General Public License

questions.explanation: GPL stands for GNU General Public License, a widely used free-software licence that grants specified rights to use, study, modify and redistribute software under its terms.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How is utility software usually classified in textbooks?

options.A: Usually taught as a subcategory of system software, but textbooks may classify it separately for convenience

questions.explanation: Utility software is usually taught as a subcategory of system software, but textbooks may classify it separately for convenience.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Technically, what does Linux refer to?

options.A: The kernel; Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora are examples of complete Linux distributions
options.B: A complete operating system with all applications

questions.explanation: Linux technically refers to the kernel; Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora are examples of complete Linux distributions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
