questions.question: How are a compiler, interpreter and assembler commonly classified?

options.A: As language-translation tools and commonly classified as system software

questions.explanation: A compiler, interpreter and assembler are language-translation tools and are commonly classified as system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What do the labels freeware, shareware and open source describe?

options.A: Different licensing or distribution characteristics; free of cost does not automatically mean open source
options.B: The same thing in all cases

questions.explanation: The labels freeware, shareware and open source describe different licensing or distribution characteristics; free of cost does not automatically mean open source.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can the categories of operating systems overlap?

options.A: Yes, for example an operating system can be multi-user, multitasking and multiprocessing at the same time
options.B: No, an operating system can belong to only one category
options.C: Yes, but only multi-user and multitasking can overlap
options.D: No, categories are always mutually exclusive

questions.explanation: The categories of operating systems can overlap. For example, an operating system can be multi-user, multitasking and multiprocessing at the same time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does software control in a computer?

options.A: Hardware operations and resource management

questions.explanation: Software provides the instructions that make hardware useful. It controls hardware operations, manages resources and enables users to perform tasks such as writing documents, calculations and communication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is true about hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware performs operations under the direction of software, and software requires hardware to execute
options.C: Hardware and software are the same thing
options.D: Software is physical and hardware is non-physical

questions.explanation: Hardware performs operations under the direction of software, and software requires hardware to execute.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is freeware necessarily open source?

options.A: No, freeware is not necessarily open source; its source code and modification rights may remain restricted
options.B: Yes, all freeware is open source
options.C: Yes, freeware always provides source code

questions.explanation: Freeware is software made available for use without a purchase price. Freeware is not necessarily open source; its source code and modification rights may remain restricted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does a software licence set out?

options.A: The conditions under which software may be installed, used, copied, modified or distributed

questions.explanation: A software licence is a legal agreement that sets out the conditions under which software may be installed, used, copied, modified or distributed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of software updating?

options.A: To fix defects, improve security, add features or maintain compatibility
options.B: To delete all files from the computer
options.D: To change the operating system permanently

questions.explanation: Software updating is the process of replacing or modifying installed software components to fix defects, improve security, add features or maintain compatibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of version numbers in software?

options.A: To help users distinguish releases and determine compatibility or update status
options.B: To increase the size of the software

questions.explanation: Version numbers help users distinguish releases and determine compatibility or update status.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the kernel of an operating system manage?

options.A: Core functions such as processes, memory, files and devices

questions.explanation: The kernel is the central component of an operating system. It manages core functions such as processes, memory, files and devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shell in an operating system?

options.A: A user interface or command interpreter through which users or programs request operating-system services
options.B: A physical case that holds the computer

questions.explanation: A shell is a user interface or command interpreter through which users or programs request operating-system services. It may be command-line based or graphical, depending on the system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a traditional compiler and an interpreter?

options.A: A traditional compiler translates source code into a target program or object code before execution, whereas an interpreter carries out program instructions at runtime
options.B: A compiler executes code at runtime and an interpreter translates before execution
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A compiler is hardware and an interpreter is software

questions.explanation: A traditional compiler translates source code into a target program or object code before execution, whereas an interpreter carries out program instructions at runtime. Modern language implementations may combine compilation and interpretation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a database-management system?

options.A: MySQL

questions.explanation: Database application software is used to create, store, organise, retrieve and manage structured data. Examples include database-management systems such as Microsoft Access, MySQL and PostgreSQL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used by email clients to access email?

options.A: IMAP

questions.explanation: An email client may access email through protocols or services such as IMAP, POP3 and SMTP.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of enterprise resource planning (ERP) software?

options.A: To integrate major organisational processes and data, such as finance, procurement, inventory, production and human resources, within a coordinated software system

questions.explanation: ERP stands for Enterprise Resource Planning. An ERP system integrates major organisational processes and data, such as finance, procurement, inventory, production and human resources, within a coordinated software system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does encryption software convert plaintext into?

options.A: Ciphertext

questions.explanation: Encryption software converts readable data (plaintext) into an encoded form (ciphertext) using a cryptographic method and key, so that only authorised parties with the required key can decrypt it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which compression type is commonly lossless?

options.A: ZIP

questions.explanation: ZIP is commonly lossless; JPEG image compression is commonly lossy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which compression type is commonly lossy?

options.A: JPEG

questions.explanation: JPEG image compression is commonly lossy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Do SSDs generally require traditional defragmentation?

options.A: No, SSDs generally do not require traditional defragmentation; operating systems use SSD-specific optimisation such as TRIM
options.C: Yes, SSDs require defragmentation more than HDDs
options.D: SSDs cannot be optimised at all

questions.explanation: SSDs generally do not require traditional defragmentation; operating systems use SSD-specific optimisation such as TRIM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does virtual memory make secondary storage as fast as RAM?

options.A: No, virtual memory does not make storage as fast as RAM
options.B: Yes, virtual memory makes storage as fast as RAM
options.C: Yes, virtual memory replaces RAM completely
options.D: Virtual memory is faster than RAM

questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory-management technique that gives processes a virtual address space and allows the operating system to use secondary storage as backing for some memory contents when needed. It does not make storage as fast as RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file system?

options.A: The method and data structure an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device

questions.explanation: A file system is the method and data structure an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device. Examples include FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, ext4 and APFS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens during booting of an operating system?

options.A: Firmware initialises hardware, identifies a bootable device and starts a bootloader or operating-system loader, which loads the operating system into memory
options.B: The operating system is deleted from memory

questions.explanation: Booting is the startup process in which firmware initialises hardware, identifies a bootable device and starts a bootloader or operating-system loader, which loads the operating system into memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a system call used for?

options.A: To request a service from the operating-system kernel, such as file access, process creation or memory management

questions.explanation: A system call is a controlled interface through which an application requests a service from the operating-system kernel, such as file access, process creation or memory management.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does a time-sharing operating system provide?

options.A: Interactive access by allocating short CPU time slices among users or processes
options.B: Batch processing with no user interaction

questions.explanation: A time-sharing operating system divides processor time into small intervals and allocates them among multiple users or processes, providing interactive access and the appearance of simultaneous execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a Linux distribution?

options.A: Ubuntu

questions.explanation: A Linux distribution is an operating-system package built around the Linux kernel. Examples include Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Linux Mint.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which operating system is based on Darwin, which includes a Unix-derived foundation?

options.A: macOS

questions.explanation: macOS is Apple's proprietary desktop operating system for Mac computers. It is based on Darwin, which includes a Unix-derived foundation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the risk of downloading drivers from unknown websites?

options.A: Malware, incompatibility and incorrect installation

questions.explanation: Drivers should be obtained from the device manufacturer, computer manufacturer or a trusted operating-system update service to reduce the risk of malware, incompatibility and incorrect installation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between a Trojan horse and a worm?

options.A: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software and does not inherently self-replicate; a worm can self-replicate and spread independently
options.B: A Trojan horse self-replicates; a worm does not
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: A Trojan horse is hardware; a worm is software

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software to deceive users and does not inherently self-replicate; a worm can self-replicate and spread independently across systems or networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between authentication and authorisation?

options.A: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines the permissions granted to that identity
options.B: Authentication determines permissions; authorisation verifies identity
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Authentication is for hardware; authorisation is for software

questions.explanation: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines the permissions granted to that identity.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between a multi-user and a multitasking operating system?

options.A: Multi-user describes support for multiple users, while multitasking describes the ability to manage multiple tasks or programs; an operating system can support both
options.B: Multi-user describes the ability to manage multiple tasks; multitasking describes support for multiple users
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Multi-user is for mobile devices; multitasking is for servers

questions.explanation: Multi-user describes support for multiple users, while multitasking describes the ability to manage multiple tasks or programs. An operating system can support both.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between batch processing and time-sharing?

options.A: Batch processing runs collected jobs with little user interaction during execution; time-sharing provides interactive access by allocating short CPU time slices among users or processes
options.B: Batch processing provides interactive access; time-sharing runs collected jobs with little user interaction
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Batch processing is for mobile devices; time-sharing is for servers

questions.explanation: Batch processing runs collected jobs with little user interaction during execution; time-sharing provides interactive access by allocating short CPU time slices among users or processes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between multitasking and multiprocessing?

options.A: Multitasking is the management of multiple tasks so they make progress during the same period; multiprocessing uses multiple processing units or cores to execute work concurrently
options.B: Multitasking uses multiple processors; multiprocessing manages multiple tasks on a single processor
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Multitasking is for mobile devices; multiprocessing is for servers

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the management of multiple tasks so they make progress during the same period; multiprocessing uses multiple processing units or cores to execute work concurrently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between freeware and open-source software?

options.A: Freeware is available without a purchase price but may have closed source and restrictive terms; open-source software provides source-code access and rights defined by its licence
options.B: Freeware provides source code; open-source software does not
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: Freeware is always open source; open-source software is always paid

questions.explanation: Freeware is available without a purchase price but may have closed source and restrictive terms; open-source software provides source-code access and rights defined by its licence.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between an update and an upgrade?

options.A: An update generally applies fixes, security improvements or smaller enhancements to an existing version; an upgrade usually moves to a newer major version or a more substantial release
options.B: An update moves to a new major version; an upgrade applies small fixes
options.C: There is no difference between them
options.D: An update is for hardware; an upgrade is for software

questions.explanation: An update generally applies fixes, security improvements or smaller enhancements to an existing version; an upgrade usually moves to a newer major version or a more substantial release. Vendors may use these terms differently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does BIOS stand for and what is its role?

options.A: Basic Input/Output System; motherboard firmware used to initialise hardware and begin the boot process
options.B: Binary Input Output Software; used for word processing
options.C: Basic Internal Operating System; used for browsing
options.D: Boot Input Output Service; used for printing

questions.explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input/Output System. It is motherboard firmware used to initialise hardware and begin the boot process; modern systems commonly use UEFI.
